ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has three JK flip-flops FF0, FF1, FF2, with outputs labeled Q0, Q1, Q2 respectively; the clock terminals of the three flip-flops are connected to the same CP line, so it is a synchronous circuit; below there is also a common clear/reset line. The J and K inputs of FF0 are connected to constant 1, making the least significant bit toggle every clock. The J/K inputs of FF1 and FF2 are obtained from the related signals Q0, Q1, Q2 by the AND-gate feedback network in the figure. Reasoning: According to the connections in the figure, it can be equivalent to FF0 toggling every clock; FF1 toggles when Q0=1 and Q2=0; the set/toggle condition of FF2 is provided by Q0·Q1, and the reset condition is provided by Q0. Using the JK flip-flop rules, calculate clock by clock from the initial state Q2Q1Q0=000: 000 → 001; at 001, Q0=1 and Q2=0, FF1 toggles, giving 010; 010 → 011; at 011, FF1 toggles and FF2 toggles, giving 100; 100 → 101; at 101, FF2 is reset and Q0 toggles, returning to 000. Therefore there are six reachable states in total: 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, and the circuit is a synchronous modulo-6 up counter.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a three-stage synchronous JK counter with LSB FF0 always toggling, FF1 toggling only under its AND-gated carry/feedback condition, and FF2 changing only when the lower-bit carry and feedback conditions demand it. Interpret these as a truncated 3-bit up-counter: it advances through the ordinary binary states 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, but the feedback logic blocks the transition into the states 110/111 and returns the machine to 000. Therefore the number of states in one counting cycle is 6.
